arcs.private.notice: Private canvas. Only you and your co-authors can see it. Insert a template or add your own cards.
arcs.empty.description: Start from a structure like the Hero's Journey, or add your own cards.
arcs.insert.description: Adds one group per stage to this canvas, each with an empty note card. Cards you already have stay where they are.
arcs.insert.info: Stage names and hints come with the template. You can rename, move or delete any group afterwards.
arcs.change.title: Change to {name}?
arcs.change.kept: {count, plural, one {Your written stage stays on the canvas. It moves} other {Your # written stages stay on the canvas. They move}} into a group called {group}, so you can drag the notes into the new stages.
arcs.change.removed: {count, plural, one {The empty stage is removed.} other {The # empty stages are removed.}}
arcs.shape.title: Shape
arcs.shape.intro: How fortunes rise and fall over the story. The first six are the shapes Reagan and colleagues found in Project Gutenberg fiction in 2016. The next six come from Kurt Vonnegut's talks on the shapes of stories. The rest are character arc types.
arcs.link.weiland: K.M. Weiland on writing character arcs
arcs.link.saveTheCat: Blake Snyder's beat sheets on savethecat.com
arcs.link.campbell: The Hero with a Thousand Faces on Wikipedia
arcs.link.reagan: The emotional arcs of stories are dominated by six basic shapes (Reagan and colleagues, 2016)
arcs.template.heroesJourney.name: Hero's Journey
arcs.template.heroesJourney.summary: Christopher Vogler's version. The hero leaves the ordinary world, is tested and returns changed.
arcs.template.heroinesJourney.name: Heroine's Journey
arcs.template.heroinesJourney.summary: Maureen Murdock's model of a journey away from the self and back to wholeness.
arcs.template.positiveChange.name: Positive change arc
arcs.template.positiveChange.summary: Your character gives up a Lie and embraces the Truth.
arcs.template.flat.name: Flat arc
arcs.template.flat.summary: Your character already knows the Truth and changes the world around them.
arcs.template.negativeChange.name: Negative change arc
arcs.template.negativeChange.summary: Your character falls, is corrupted or loses their illusions.
arcs.template.monomyth.name: Campbell's monomyth
arcs.template.monomyth.summary: Joseph Campbell's original stages from The Hero with a Thousand Faces.
arcs.template.threeAct.name: Three-act structure
arcs.template.saveTheCat.name: Save the Cat!
arcs.template.storyCircle.name: Story Circle
arcs.template.storyCircle.summary: Dan Harmon's steps of going out and coming back changed.
arcs.template.freytag.name: Freytag's pyramid
arcs.template.sevenPoint.name: Seven-point structure
arcs.template.sevenPoint.summary: Dan Wells' structure, planned from the ending back.
arcs.template.fichtean.name: Fichtean curve
arcs.template.fichtean.summary: A series of crises that build to the climax.
arcs.template.kishotenketsu.name: Kishōtenketsu
arcs.template.kishotenketsu.summary: Four parts built around a twist instead of a conflict.
arcs.template.storySpine.name: Story Spine
arcs.template.storySpine.summary: Kenn Adams' sentence starters, made popular by Pixar.
arcs.template.fourAct.name: Four-act structure
arcs.template.fourAct.summary: Larry Brooks' model. Four equal parts with a major turn between each.
arcs.template.eightSequence.name: Eight-sequence structure
arcs.template.eightSequence.summary: Frank Daniel's film model. Three acts split into eight short sequences.
arcs.template.sixStage.name: Six-stage plot structure
arcs.template.sixStage.summary: Michael Hauge's screenplay model. Five turning points divide the outer and inner journey.
arcs.template.truby.name: Truby's 22 steps
arcs.template.truby.summary: John Truby's detailed steps from The Anatomy of Story.
arcs.template.proppFunctions.name: Propp's functions
arcs.template.proppFunctions.summary: Vladimir Propp's 31 functions, drawn from Russian folk tales. Use the ones your story needs.
arcs.template.bookerMetaPlot.name: Booker's meta-plot
arcs.template.bookerMetaPlot.summary: The five stages Christopher Booker found under his seven basic plots.
arcs.shape.ragsToRiches.name: Rags to riches
arcs.shape.richesToRags.name: Riches to rags
arcs.shape.manInAHole.name: Man in a hole
arcs.shape.icarus.name: Icarus
arcs.shape.cinderella.name: Cinderella
arcs.shape.cinderella.summary: A rise, a fall and a rise again.
arcs.shape.oedipus.name: Oedipus
arcs.shape.oedipus.summary: A fall, a rise and a fall again.
arcs.shape.boyMeetsGirl.name: Boy meets girl
arcs.shape.boyMeetsGirl.summary: Good luck arrives, is lost and is won back.
arcs.shape.fromBadToWorse.name: From bad to worse
arcs.shape.fromBadToWorse.summary: A poor start that keeps sinking.
arcs.shape.whichWayIsUp.name: Which way is up?
arcs.shape.whichWayIsUp.summary: Things happen, and nobody can say if they are good or bad.
arcs.shape.creationStory.name: Creation story
arcs.shape.creationStory.summary: Gifts arrive one after another, in steps.
arcs.shape.oldTestament.name: Old Testament
arcs.shape.oldTestament.summary: Gifts arrive in steps, then a sudden fall.
arcs.shape.newTestament.name: New Testament
arcs.shape.newTestament.summary: The same sudden fall, then a rise higher than ever.
arcs.shape.positiveChange.name: Positive change
arcs.shape.positiveChange.summary: The character grows into someone better.
arcs.shape.flat.name: Flat
arcs.shape.flat.summary: The character stays true while the world around them changes.
arcs.shape.disillusionment.name: Disillusionment
arcs.shape.disillusionment.summary: The character learns a hard truth and is hurt by it.
arcs.shape.fall.name: Fall
arcs.shape.fall.summary: The character trades one lie for a worse one.
arcs.shape.corruption.name: Corruption
arcs.shape.corruption.summary: The character starts with the truth and gives it up.
arcs.shape.custom.name: Custom
arcs.shape.custom.summary: Draw your own curve. Each slider sets one point of the story.
arcs.stage.ordinaryWorld.name: Ordinary World
arcs.stage.ordinaryWorld.hint: Show the hero's everyday life before the adventure. It sets up what they lack and what they stand to lose.
arcs.stage.ordinaryWorld.ask:
What does a normal day look like for your character?
What is missing from their life?
What would they hate to lose?
arcs.stage.callToAdventure.name: Call to Adventure
arcs.stage.callToAdventure.hint: Something disrupts the ordinary world and offers a challenge, a quest or a problem the hero cannot ignore.
arcs.stage.callToAdventure.ask:
What event or message starts the story?
Why does it reach your character now?
arcs.stage.refusalOfTheCall.name: Refusal of the Call
arcs.stage.refusalOfTheCall.hint: The hero hesitates. Fear, duty or doubt holds them back, and the reader sees what the journey will cost.
arcs.stage.refusalOfTheCall.ask:
What is your character afraid of?
What or who keeps them at home?
arcs.stage.meetingTheMentor.name: Meeting the Mentor
arcs.stage.meetingTheMentor.hint: Someone or something gives the hero advice, training, a gift or the confidence to go.
arcs.stage.meetingTheMentor.ask:
Who believes in your character?
What do they give, and what do they hold back?
arcs.stage.crossingTheThreshold.name: Crossing the Threshold
arcs.stage.crossingTheThreshold.hint: The hero commits and leaves the familiar world for the unknown. There is no easy way back.
arcs.stage.crossingTheThreshold.ask:
What makes the decision final?
How is the new world different from the old one?
arcs.stage.testsAlliesEnemies.name: Tests, Allies, Enemies
arcs.stage.testsAlliesEnemies.hint: In the new world the hero learns its rules, makes friends and enemies, and faces smaller tests.
arcs.stage.testsAlliesEnemies.ask:
Who joins your character, and who works against them?
Which skill or belief is tested first?
arcs.stage.approach.name: Approach to the Inmost Cave
arcs.stage.approach.hint: The hero and their allies prepare for the central danger. They make plans, and the tension builds.
arcs.stage.approach.ask:
What is the inmost cave in your story?
Which doubts return as the danger gets closer?
arcs.stage.ordeal.name: The Ordeal
arcs.stage.ordeal.hint: The hero faces their greatest fear or a life-or-death crisis. Something must die here, whether an old belief, a relationship or the hero's former self.
arcs.stage.ordeal.ask:
What does your character stand to lose?
Which flaw from the Ordinary World is tested here?
How is the character changed afterwards?
arcs.stage.reward.name: Reward
arcs.stage.reward.hint: The hero survives and takes the reward. It can be an object, knowledge or a reconciliation.
arcs.stage.reward.ask:
What does your character gain?
What does the victory cost them?
arcs.stage.roadBack.name: The Road Back
arcs.stage.roadBack.hint: The hero heads for home, often chased by the consequences of the ordeal. A new problem forces a final commitment.
arcs.stage.roadBack.ask:
What pursues your character?
Why can't they simply go home?
arcs.stage.resurrection.name: Resurrection
arcs.stage.resurrection.hint: A final, most dangerous test on the threshold of home. The hero uses everything they have learned and comes out reborn.
arcs.stage.resurrection.ask:
How is the final test different from the ordeal?
What proves your character has changed?
arcs.stage.returnWithElixir.name: Return with the Elixir
arcs.stage.returnWithElixir.hint: The hero comes home with something that changes the ordinary world, such as wisdom, a treasure or new freedom.
arcs.stage.returnWithElixir.ask:
What does your character bring back?
How has the ordinary world changed, and how have they?
arcs.stage.separationFromFeminine.name: Separation from the Feminine
arcs.stage.separationFromFeminine.hint: Your character turns away from what they see as feminine, often from their mother, to find their own way.
arcs.stage.separationFromFeminine.ask:
What does your character reject about where they come from?
What do they hope to find instead?
arcs.stage.identificationWithMasculine.h: Your character takes on values seen as masculine, such as achievement and independence, and gathers allies.
arcs.stage.identificationWithMasculine.a:
Whose approval does your character want?
Who helps them succeed?
arcs.stage.roadOfTrials.name: Road of Trials
arcs.stage.roadOfTrials.hint: Your character faces a series of tests and enemies. They fail some of them, and each one changes them a little.
arcs.stage.roadOfTrials.ask:
What are the hardest tests?
What does failing one teach your character?
arcs.stage.illusoryBoon.name: The Illusory Boon of Success
arcs.stage.illusoryBoon.hint: Your character gets what they worked for, yet it feels hollow.
arcs.stage.illusoryBoon.ask:
What success does your character reach?
Why isn't it enough?
arcs.stage.spiritualAridity.name: Spiritual Aridity
arcs.stage.spiritualAridity.hint: A sense of emptiness or betrayal sets in. The old way of living no longer works.
arcs.stage.spiritualAridity.ask:
What makes your character feel empty?
What do they lose here?
arcs.stage.descentToGoddess.name: Descent to the Goddess
arcs.stage.descentToGoddess.hint: Your character goes through a dark time of loss, grief or isolation, and meets a deeper part of themselves.
arcs.stage.descentToGoddess.ask:
What is your character's darkest moment?
What do they discover there?
arcs.stage.yearningForFeminine.name: Yearning to Reconnect with the Feminine
arcs.stage.yearningForFeminine.hint: Your character longs to recover the parts of themselves they rejected, such as feeling, intuition or care.
arcs.stage.yearningForFeminine.ask:
What did your character give up at the start?
What makes them want it back?
arcs.stage.motherDaughterSplit.name: Healing the Mother/Daughter Split
arcs.stage.motherDaughterSplit.hint: Your character makes peace with the feminine they turned away from, often through a mother figure.
arcs.stage.motherDaughterSplit.ask:
Who or what does your character reconcile with?
What makes the reconciliation possible?
arcs.stage.woundedMasculine.name: Healing the Wounded Masculine
arcs.stage.woundedMasculine.hint: Your character keeps the strengths of the masculine values they took on and lets go of their harshness.
arcs.stage.woundedMasculine.ask:
Which strengths does your character keep?
What do they stop demanding of themselves?
arcs.stage.integration.name: Integration of Masculine and Feminine
arcs.stage.integration.hint: Your character becomes whole and can draw on both sides of themselves.
arcs.stage.integration.ask:
How does your character act differently now?
What shows that they are whole?
arcs.stage.lieBelieved.name: The Lie
arcs.stage.lieBelieved.hint: A false belief your character holds about themselves or the world. What they want grows out of it.
arcs.stage.lieBelieved.ask:
What does your character believe that isn't true?
Where did they learn it?
How does it hold them back?
arcs.stage.ghost.name: The Ghost
arcs.stage.ghost.hint: A past event or wound that gave birth to your character's belief. Other characters often don't know about it.
arcs.stage.ghost.ask:
What happened to your character before the story?
Why do they still carry it?
arcs.stage.wantVsNeed.name: Want versus Need
arcs.stage.wantVsNeed.hint: What your character wants is shaped by what they believe. What they need may be the opposite.
arcs.stage.wantVsNeed.ask:
What does your character chase?
What do they actually need?
Why can't they have both?
arcs.stage.normalWorld.name: The Normal World
arcs.stage.normalWorld.hint: Show your character's everyday life before the story changes it, and how their belief shapes that life.
arcs.stage.normalWorld.ask:
What does a normal day show about your character?
Who shares this world with them?
arcs.stage.incitingIncident.name: Inciting Incident
arcs.stage.incitingIncident.hint: An event sets the story in motion and pulls your character into the conflict.
arcs.stage.incitingIncident.ask:
What happens that your character can't ignore?
How do they react at first?
arcs.stage.momentOfTruth.name: Moment of Truth
arcs.stage.momentOfTruth.hint: At the midpoint your character glimpses the Truth but has not yet given up the Lie.
arcs.stage.momentOfTruth.ask:
What does your character finally see?
Why don't they act on it yet?
arcs.stage.darkNight.name: Dark Night
arcs.stage.darkNight.hint: The Lie and the Truth collide. Holding on to the Lie costs your character dearly.
arcs.stage.darkNight.ask:
What is your character's lowest point?
What finally makes the Lie impossible to keep?
arcs.stage.truthEmbraced.name: Truth Embraced
arcs.stage.truthEmbraced.hint: In the climax your character acts on the Truth, even at a cost.
arcs.stage.truthEmbraced.ask:
What choice proves the change?
What does it cost?
arcs.stage.newNormal.name: The New Normal
arcs.stage.newNormal.hint: Show your character's life after the change, so readers can see how far they have come.
arcs.stage.newNormal.ask:
How is this day different from the first one?
What can your character do now that they couldn't before?
arcs.stage.truthHeld.name: The Truth
arcs.stage.truthHeld.hint: Your character already believes something true and holds on to it from the start.
arcs.stage.truthHeld.ask:
What does your character know that others don't?
Where does that conviction come from?
arcs.stage.worldsLie.name: The World's Lie
arcs.stage.worldsLie.hint: The people or the world around your character believe a Lie that hurts them.
arcs.stage.worldsLie.ask:
What false belief rules this world?
Who suffers because of it?
arcs.stage.truthChallenged.name: The Truth Challenged
arcs.stage.truthChallenged.hint: The world pushes back. Standing by the Truth gets your character into trouble.
arcs.stage.truthChallenged.ask:
Who opposes your character first?
What does staying true cost?
arcs.stage.truthDoubted.name: Doubt
arcs.stage.truthDoubted.hint: Your character is tempted to give up the Truth, or doubts it for a while.
arcs.stage.truthDoubted.ask:
What makes your character waver?
Who or what reminds them why it matters?
arcs.stage.truthDefended.name: The Truth Defended
arcs.stage.truthDefended.hint: In the climax your character stands by the Truth and acts on it.
arcs.stage.truthDefended.ask:
What is the final test of your character's belief?
How do they prove it?
arcs.stage.worldChanged.name: The World Changed
arcs.stage.worldChanged.hint: Your character stays the same. The people around them or the world itself have changed.
arcs.stage.worldChanged.ask:
Who has changed because of your character?
What does the world look like now?
arcs.stage.startingBelief.name: Starting Belief
arcs.stage.startingBelief.hint: Your character starts out believing a Lie, or in a corruption arc, believing the Truth.
arcs.stage.startingBelief.ask:
What does your character believe at the start?
Is it true?
arcs.stage.wrongTurn.name: The Wrong Turn
arcs.stage.wrongTurn.hint: Your character takes a first step in the wrong direction, often a small one.
arcs.stage.wrongTurn.ask:
What tempts your character?
Why does the wrong choice look reasonable?
arcs.stage.pointOfNoReturn.name: Point of No Return
arcs.stage.pointOfNoReturn.hint: At the midpoint your character rejects the Truth or commits to the Lie.
arcs.stage.pointOfNoReturn.ask:
What does your character turn away from?
Who tries to stop them?
arcs.stage.consequences.name: Consequences
arcs.stage.consequences.hint: The cost of your character's choices grows, for them and for the people around them.
arcs.stage.consequences.ask:
Who gets hurt?
What does your character tell themselves to keep going?
arcs.stage.finalChoice.name: Final Choice
arcs.stage.finalChoice.hint: In the climax your character makes the choice that seals their fall.
arcs.stage.finalChoice.ask:
What final choice does your character make?
What could have saved them?
arcs.stage.aftermath.name: Aftermath
arcs.stage.aftermath.hint: Show what the fall has cost. In a disillusionment arc your character knows the Truth but is left hurt by it.
arcs.stage.aftermath.ask:
What has your character lost?
What should readers take away?
arcs.stage.supernaturalAid.name: Supernatural Aid
arcs.stage.supernaturalAid.hint: Once the hero commits, a protective figure appears and offers help or a magical gift.
arcs.stage.supernaturalAid.ask:
Who or what helps your character?
What do they give?
arcs.stage.bellyOfTheWhale.name: Belly of the Whale
arcs.stage.bellyOfTheWhale.hint: The unknown swallows the hero and cuts them off from the old world. Their transformation begins here.
arcs.stage.bellyOfTheWhale.ask:
Where is your character most cut off from home?
Which part of their old self ends here?
arcs.stage.meetingWithTheGoddess.name: Meeting with the Goddess
arcs.stage.meetingWithTheGoddess.hint: The hero finds an unconditional love or a deep bond that gives them strength.
arcs.stage.meetingWithTheGoddess.ask:
Who or what does your character love completely?
How does it change them?
arcs.stage.temptation.name: Temptation
arcs.stage.temptation.hint: Comforts or desires tempt the hero to abandon the quest. Campbell called this stage Woman as Temptress.
arcs.stage.temptation.ask:
What could make your character give up?
What do they resist, and how?
arcs.stage.atonementWithTheFather.name: Atonement with the Father
arcs.stage.atonementWithTheFather.hint: The hero confronts whoever holds the most power over their life, often a father figure.
arcs.stage.atonementWithTheFather.ask:
Who holds power over your character?
What do they have to face or forgive?
arcs.stage.apotheosis.name: Apotheosis
arcs.stage.apotheosis.hint: The hero reaches a new understanding, as if part of them has died and been reborn.
arcs.stage.apotheosis.ask:
What does your character finally understand?
How does it change their view of the quest?
arcs.stage.ultimateBoon.name: The Ultimate Boon
arcs.stage.ultimateBoon.hint: The hero achieves the goal of the quest.
arcs.stage.ultimateBoon.ask:
What is the boon?
What did it take to win it?
arcs.stage.refusalOfTheReturn.name: Refusal of the Return
arcs.stage.refusalOfTheReturn.hint: After finding bliss or wisdom, the hero does not want to go back.
arcs.stage.refusalOfTheReturn.ask:
Why would your character rather stay?
What pulls them home?
arcs.stage.magicFlight.name: The Magic Flight
arcs.stage.magicFlight.hint: The hero escapes with the boon, often pursued.
arcs.stage.magicFlight.ask:
Who wants the boon back?
How does your character escape?
arcs.stage.rescueFromWithout.name: Rescue from Without
arcs.stage.rescueFromWithout.hint: The hero may need help from others to get back.
arcs.stage.rescueFromWithout.ask:
Who comes for your character?
Why can't they make it alone?
arcs.stage.returnThreshold.name: Crossing the Return Threshold
arcs.stage.returnThreshold.hint: The hero brings the wisdom home and learns to share it with the ordinary world.
arcs.stage.returnThreshold.ask:
How does home receive your character?
What is hard to explain to the people there?
arcs.stage.masterOfTwoWorlds.name: Master of Two Worlds
arcs.stage.masterOfTwoWorlds.hint: The hero is at ease both in the ordinary world and in the world of the adventure.
arcs.stage.masterOfTwoWorlds.ask:
How does your character move between the two worlds?
What balance have they found?
arcs.stage.freedomToLive.name: Freedom to Live
arcs.stage.freedomToLive.hint: Free of the fear of death or failure, the hero lives in the moment.
arcs.stage.freedomToLive.ask:
What is your character no longer afraid of?
How do they live now?
arcs.stage.actSetup.name: Act I: Setup
arcs.stage.actSetup.hint: Introduce the characters, their world and what they want. End the act with an event that commits them to the conflict.
arcs.stage.actSetup.ask:
What does your reader need to know first?
Which event ends the setup?
arcs.stage.actConfrontation.name: Act II: Confrontation
arcs.stage.actConfrontation.hint: Your characters chase their goal against growing obstacles. A turn at the midpoint raises the stakes, and the act ends at the lowest point.
arcs.stage.actConfrontation.ask:
What stands in the way?
What changes at the midpoint?
What is the lowest point?
arcs.stage.actResolution.name: Act III: Resolution
arcs.stage.actResolution.hint: The conflict reaches its climax and is resolved. Show the new state of the world.
arcs.stage.actResolution.ask:
How does the climax play out?
What has changed for good?
arcs.stage.openingImage.name: Opening Image
arcs.stage.openingImage.hint: A single scene that shows the hero's world and problem before anything changes.
arcs.stage.openingImage.ask:
Which image sums up your hero's life now?
How will the final image mirror it?
arcs.stage.themeStated.name: Theme Stated
arcs.stage.themeStated.hint: Someone, usually not the hero, hints at the lesson the hero needs to learn.
arcs.stage.themeStated.ask:
What is the story really about?
Who says it, and does the hero listen?
arcs.stage.setUp.name: Set-Up
arcs.stage.setUp.hint: Show the hero's world, the people in it and what needs fixing in the hero's life.
arcs.stage.setUp.ask:
Which flaws or problems will the story address?
Who are the important characters?
arcs.stage.catalyst.name: Catalyst
arcs.stage.catalyst.hint: Something happens that changes the hero's life and starts the story.
arcs.stage.catalyst.ask:
What is the life-changing event?
Why does it happen now?
arcs.stage.debate.name: Debate
arcs.stage.debate.hint: The hero doubts the journey ahead and asks whether to go.
arcs.stage.debate.ask:
What does your hero fear?
What would happen if they stayed?
arcs.stage.breakIntoTwo.name: Break into Two
arcs.stage.breakIntoTwo.hint: The hero chooses to act and enters a new world or situation.
arcs.stage.breakIntoTwo.ask:
Which choice does the hero make?
How is the new world the opposite of the old one?
arcs.stage.bStory.name: B Story
arcs.stage.bStory.hint: A second storyline begins, often a relationship, and carries the theme.
arcs.stage.bStory.ask:
Who helps the hero learn the theme?
How does this storyline support the main one?
arcs.stage.funAndGames.name: Fun and Games
arcs.stage.funAndGames.hint: The promise of the premise. The hero explores the new world, succeeding or struggling.
arcs.stage.funAndGames.ask:
Which scenes would readers expect from your premise?
Is the hero winning or losing?
arcs.stage.midpoint.name: Midpoint
arcs.stage.midpoint.hint: A false victory or a false defeat raises the stakes. Your character stops reacting and starts acting.
arcs.stage.midpoint.ask:
What changes at the midpoint?
What does your character decide to do about it?
arcs.stage.badGuysCloseIn.name: Bad Guys Close In
arcs.stage.badGuysCloseIn.hint: Enemies outside regroup, and doubts inside the hero's team grow.
arcs.stage.badGuysCloseIn.ask:
How do the opponents strike back?
Which cracks appear among the allies?
arcs.stage.allIsLost.name: All Is Lost
arcs.stage.allIsLost.hint: The lowest moment. Something or someone is lost, and the hero's old way of life dies.
arcs.stage.allIsLost.ask:
What does the hero lose?
Which old belief dies here?
arcs.stage.darkNightOfTheSoul.name: Dark Night of the Soul
arcs.stage.darkNightOfTheSoul.hint: The hero reacts to the loss and hits rock bottom before finding the answer.
arcs.stage.darkNightOfTheSoul.ask:
How does the hero grieve?
What realization lifts them?
arcs.stage.breakIntoThree.name: Break into Three
arcs.stage.breakIntoThree.hint: Thanks to the B story and the lesson learned, the hero finds the solution.
arcs.stage.breakIntoThree.ask:
What finally clicks?
How do the A and B stories come together?
arcs.stage.finale.name: Finale
arcs.stage.finale.hint: The hero puts the lesson into practice, defeats the problem and changes their world.
arcs.stage.finale.ask:
How does the hero prove the change?
What does the final confrontation look like?
arcs.stage.finalImage.name: Final Image
arcs.stage.finalImage.hint: A mirror of the opening image that shows how much has changed.
arcs.stage.finalImage.ask:
How does this image echo the opening one?
What does it say about the hero now?
arcs.stage.circleYou.name: You
arcs.stage.circleYou.hint: Your character is in a zone of comfort.
arcs.stage.circleYou.ask:
Who is your character, and where are they comfortable?
What does a normal day look like?
arcs.stage.circleNeed.name: Need
arcs.stage.circleNeed.ask:
What does your character want?
Why can't they get it where they are?
arcs.stage.circleGo.name: Go
arcs.stage.circleGo.ask:
Which new place or situation do they enter?
What makes them go?
arcs.stage.circleSearch.name: Search
arcs.stage.circleSearch.hint: They adapt to it and struggle along the way.
arcs.stage.circleSearch.ask:
What rules does the new situation have?
What does your character struggle with?
arcs.stage.circleFind.name: Find
arcs.stage.circleFind.ask:
What does your character find?
Is it what they expected?
arcs.stage.circleTake.name: Take
arcs.stage.circleTake.hint: They pay a heavy price for it.
arcs.stage.circleTake.ask:
What does it cost?
Who else pays?
arcs.stage.circleReturn.name: Return
arcs.stage.circleReturn.hint: They go back to their familiar situation.
arcs.stage.circleReturn.ask:
How does your character get back?
What do they bring with them?
arcs.stage.circleChange.name: Change
arcs.stage.circleChange.hint: They have changed. Show the difference.
arcs.stage.circleChange.ask:
How is your character different now?
How does their old life look to them?
arcs.stage.exposition.name: Exposition
arcs.stage.exposition.hint: Introduce the setting, the characters and the situation before the conflict starts.
arcs.stage.exposition.ask:
What does your reader need to know?
What hints at the coming conflict?
arcs.stage.risingAction.name: Rising Action
arcs.stage.risingAction.hint: A series of events builds the conflict and the tension toward the climax.
arcs.stage.risingAction.ask:
Which events raise the stakes?
How does each one make things harder?
arcs.stage.climax.name: Climax
arcs.stage.climax.hint: The turning point of highest tension, where the conflict comes to a head.
arcs.stage.climax.ask:
What is the decisive moment?
Which choice does your character make?
arcs.stage.fallingAction.name: Falling Action
arcs.stage.fallingAction.hint: The results of the climax play out, and loose ends start to tie up.
arcs.stage.fallingAction.ask:
What follows from the climax?
Which threads still need resolving?
arcs.stage.denouement.name: Dénouement
arcs.stage.denouement.hint: The conflict is resolved, for better or worse. In a tragedy this is the catastrophe.
arcs.stage.denouement.ask:
How does the story end for each character?
What feeling should the reader leave with?
arcs.stage.hook.name: Hook
arcs.stage.hook.hint: Show your character's starting state, the opposite of where they end up.
arcs.stage.hook.ask:
Where does your character start?
How is it the opposite of the resolution?
arcs.stage.plotTurnOne.name: Plot Turn 1
arcs.stage.plotTurnOne.hint: An event brings in the conflict and moves your character from the starting state toward the story's goal.
arcs.stage.plotTurnOne.ask:
What sets the story in motion?
Which new idea or goal does it bring?
arcs.stage.pinchOne.name: Pinch 1
arcs.stage.pinchOne.hint: Pressure from the antagonist forces your character to act.
arcs.stage.pinchOne.ask:
How does the opposition show its strength?
What does your character do about it?
arcs.stage.pinchTwo.name: Pinch 2
arcs.stage.pinchTwo.hint: More pressure. A plan fails or an ally is lost, and everything seems lost.
arcs.stage.pinchTwo.ask:
What goes wrong?
What does your character lose?
arcs.stage.plotTurnTwo.name: Plot Turn 2
arcs.stage.plotTurnTwo.hint: Your character finds the last piece they need to resolve the conflict.
arcs.stage.plotTurnTwo.ask:
What does your character discover or gain?
How does it make the resolution possible?
arcs.stage.resolution.name: Resolution
arcs.stage.resolution.hint: The climax. Your character resolves the conflict and reaches the end state.
arcs.stage.resolution.ask:
How is the conflict resolved?
How far has your character come since the hook?
arcs.stage.firstCrisis.name: First Crisis
arcs.stage.firstCrisis.hint: The first serious obstacle. Your character overcomes it, but the tension does not drop.
arcs.stage.firstCrisis.ask:
What is the first crisis?
How does solving it make things worse?
arcs.stage.secondCrisis.name: Second Crisis
arcs.stage.secondCrisis.hint: A bigger crisis builds on the first and raises the stakes again.
arcs.stage.secondCrisis.ask:
How is this crisis bigger?
What does your character learn from it?
arcs.stage.thirdCrisis.name: Third Crisis
arcs.stage.thirdCrisis.hint: The biggest crisis yet leads straight into the climax.
arcs.stage.thirdCrisis.ask:
What makes this crisis the hardest?
How does it set up the climax?
arcs.stage.ki.name: Ki: Introduction
arcs.stage.ki.hint: Introduce the characters and the setting.
arcs.stage.ki.ask:
Who is the story about, and where does it happen?
What is ordinary here?
arcs.stage.sho.name: Shō: Development
arcs.stage.sho.hint: Develop what you introduced, without a major change.
arcs.stage.sho.ask:
What do readers learn about the characters?
Which routine or pattern forms?
arcs.stage.ten.name: Ten: Twist
arcs.stage.ten.hint: An unexpected turn or new element changes how readers see everything before it. It does not have to be a conflict.
arcs.stage.ten.ask:
Which surprising element enters?
How does it change the meaning of the first two parts?
arcs.stage.ketsu.name: Ketsu: Conclusion
arcs.stage.ketsu.hint: Bring the parts together and show how the twist connects to the beginning.
arcs.stage.ketsu.ask:
How do the parts fit together now?
What is the reader left with?
arcs.stage.onceUponATime.name: Once upon a time…
arcs.stage.onceUponATime.hint: Introduce the main character and their world.
arcs.stage.onceUponATime.ask:
Who is this story about?
Where and when does it happen?
arcs.stage.everyDay.name: Every day…
arcs.stage.everyDay.hint: Show the routine before anything changes.
arcs.stage.everyDay.ask:
What does your character do every day?
What balance does the routine keep?
arcs.stage.oneDay.name: One day…
arcs.stage.oneDay.ask:
What changes?
Why can't your character ignore it?
arcs.stage.becauseOfThat.name: Because of that…
arcs.stage.becauseOfThat.hint: The first consequence of the change.
arcs.stage.becauseOfThat.ask:
What happens as a result?
What does your character do?
arcs.stage.becauseOfThatAgain.name: Because of that…
arcs.stage.becauseOfThatAgain.hint: More consequences pile up, each caused by the one before.
arcs.stage.becauseOfThatAgain.ask:
What follows from the last event?
How do the stakes grow?
arcs.stage.untilFinally.name: Until finally…
arcs.stage.untilFinally.hint: The climax that settles the story.
arcs.stage.untilFinally.ask:
What ends the chain of events?
What does your character finally do?
arcs.stage.everSinceThen.name: And ever since then…
arcs.stage.everSinceThen.hint: Show the new routine and what it means.
arcs.stage.everSinceThen.ask:
What is the new normal?
Is there a moral to the story?
arcs.stage.fourActSetup.name: Setup
arcs.stage.fourActSetup.hint: Introduce the hero, the stakes and the world before the main conflict arrives. End this part with the event that changes the hero's path.
arcs.stage.fourActSetup.ask:
What does your hero want at the start?
What do they stand to lose?
Which event ends normal life?
arcs.stage.fourActResponse.name: Response
arcs.stage.fourActResponse.hint: The hero reacts. They run, hide, regroup or look for answers, without yet understanding what they face.
arcs.stage.fourActResponse.ask:
How does your hero react first?
What do they get wrong?
What do they learn at the midpoint?
arcs.stage.fourActAttack.name: Attack
arcs.stage.fourActAttack.hint: Since the midpoint the hero has stopped reacting. They go after the problem with a plan, and it costs them.
arcs.stage.fourActAttack.ask:
What is your hero's plan?
What does it cost them?
Which new piece of information changes everything?
arcs.stage.fourActResolution.name: Resolution
arcs.stage.fourActResolution.hint: The hero solves the problem through their own choices and courage. Tie up the threads and show who they have become.
arcs.stage.fourActResolution.ask:
What does your hero do that only they could do?
What has changed in them?
arcs.stage.seqStatusQuo.name: Status Quo and Inciting Incident
arcs.stage.seqStatusQuo.hint: Show the hero's life as it is, then disturb it. By the end of this sequence something has happened that can't be ignored.
arcs.stage.seqStatusQuo.ask:
What is normal for your hero?
What disturbs it?
arcs.stage.seqPredicament.name: Predicament and Lock-in
arcs.stage.seqPredicament.hint: The hero tries to avoid the problem or fix it cheaply, and fails. The sequence ends when they are locked into the story's main task.
arcs.stage.seqPredicament.ask:
What does your hero try first?
What leaves them no way back?
arcs.stage.seqFirstObstacle.name: First Obstacle and Raising the Stakes
arcs.stage.seqFirstObstacle.hint: The hero's first real attempt meets its first serious obstacle. What they stand to lose grows.
arcs.stage.seqFirstObstacle.ask:
What is the simplest plan your hero would try?
What blocks it?
What is at risk now that wasn't before?
arcs.stage.seqFirstCulmination.name: First Culmination
arcs.stage.seqFirstCulmination.hint: The middle of the story. A big win or loss gives a false idea of how the story will end.
arcs.stage.seqFirstCulmination.ask:
Does your hero seem to win or lose here?
What does this make them believe about the ending?
arcs.stage.seqSubplot.name: Subplot and Rising Action
arcs.stage.seqSubplot.hint: Give time to a subplot, a relationship or the theme, while the pressure of the main task keeps building.
arcs.stage.seqSubplot.ask:
Which subplot gets its turn here?
How does it feed back into the main task?
arcs.stage.seqMainCulmination.name: Main Culmination
arcs.stage.seqMainCulmination.hint: The end of the second act. The hero reaches their lowest point or a last false victory, and the main task comes to a head.
arcs.stage.seqMainCulmination.ask:
What is the worst that can happen now?
What does your hero finally understand?
arcs.stage.seqNewTension.name: New Tension and Twist
arcs.stage.seqNewTension.hint: A new tension takes over, often a different goal or a twist that shows the hero's first aim was wrong.
arcs.stage.seqNewTension.ask:
What new goal or question drives the end of the story?
Which twist does the reader not see coming?
arcs.stage.seqResolution.name: Resolution
arcs.stage.seqResolution.hint: Settle the story's tension. Show the hero's life after the fight and what has changed.
arcs.stage.seqResolution.ask:
How is the main question answered?
What has changed since the first sequence?
arcs.stage.haugeSetup.name: Setup
arcs.stage.haugeSetup.hint: Show the hero's everyday life and the identity they hide behind. End with an opportunity that starts the story.
arcs.stage.haugeSetup.ask:
What does your hero do every day?
Who do they pretend to be?
What opportunity arrives?
arcs.stage.haugeNewSituation.name: New Situation
arcs.stage.haugeNewSituation.hint: The hero takes the opportunity and enters a new place or situation. At the end, a vague desire becomes a concrete, visible goal.
arcs.stage.haugeNewSituation.ask:
What is new for your hero here?
What exact goal do they set?
arcs.stage.haugeProgress.name: Progress
arcs.stage.haugeProgress.hint: The plan seems to work. The hero gets closer to the goal and starts to drop their old identity. End at the point of no return.
arcs.stage.haugeProgress.ask:
What goes right for your hero?
Which step can't they take back?
arcs.stage.haugeComplications.name: Complications and Higher Stakes
arcs.stage.haugeComplications.hint: The hero can't go back, and the obstacles get harder. End with a major setback that seems to take all hope away.
arcs.stage.haugeComplications.ask:
What stands in your hero's way now?
What is the major setback?
arcs.stage.haugeFinalPush.name: Final Push
arcs.stage.haugeFinalPush.hint: With nothing left to lose, the hero makes a last attempt and faces their biggest fear. End at the climax, when they reach the goal or lose it.
arcs.stage.haugeFinalPush.ask:
What does your hero risk in this last attempt?
Which fear do they finally face?
arcs.stage.haugeAftermath.name: Aftermath
arcs.stage.haugeAftermath.hint: Show the new life the hero has earned and who they are without the identity they used to hide behind.
arcs.stage.haugeAftermath.ask:
What does your hero's new life look like?
What has happened to their old identity?
arcs.stage.trubySelfRevelationNeedDesire: Start at the end. Decide what your hero will finally understand, then work out what they need and what they think they want.

What will your hero understand by the end?
What do they need but can't see?
What do they think they want?
arcs.stage.trubyGhostWorld.name: Ghost and Story World
arcs.stage.trubyGhostWorld.hint: Give the hero a wound from the past that still holds them back, and a world that presses on it.
arcs.stage.trubyGhostWorld.ask:
What past event still haunts your hero?
How does the story's world make it worse?
arcs.stage.trubyWeaknessNeed.name: Weakness and Need
arcs.stage.trubyWeaknessNeed.hint: Show the flaw that is damaging the hero's life and what they have to fix in themselves, before they know it.
arcs.stage.trubyWeaknessNeed.ask:
What flaw hurts your hero now?
Who else does it hurt?
arcs.stage.trubyIncitingEvent.name: Inciting Event
arcs.stage.trubyIncitingEvent.hint: An outside event makes the hero act and connects to their weakness.
arcs.stage.trubyIncitingEvent.ask:
What forces your hero to act?
How does it touch their weakness?
arcs.stage.trubyDesire.name: Desire
arcs.stage.trubyDesire.hint: The hero sets a specific goal. This goal is the line the reader follows through the story.
arcs.stage.trubyDesire.ask:
What exactly does your hero want?
How will the reader know if they get it?
arcs.stage.trubyAlly.name: Ally or Allies
arcs.stage.trubyAlly.hint: Give the hero people who help them and who speak up when they are wrong.
arcs.stage.trubyAlly.ask:
Who helps your hero?
Who can tell them the truth?
arcs.stage.trubyOpponent.name: Opponent and Mystery
arcs.stage.trubyOpponent.hint: Create the person who wants the same thing as the hero and who goes for their weakness. Hide something about them for the hero to find out.
arcs.stage.trubyOpponent.ask:
Why do your hero and opponent want the same thing?
What does the opponent keep hidden?
arcs.stage.trubyFakeAlly.name: Fake-Ally Opponent
arcs.stage.trubyFakeAlly.hint: Add someone who looks like a friend and works against the hero.
arcs.stage.trubyFakeAlly.ask:
Who seems to be on your hero's side?
What do they gain by betraying them?
arcs.stage.trubyChangedDesire.name: Changed Desire and Motive
arcs.stage.trubyChangedDesire.hint: The first revelation. New information changes what the hero wants and why they want it.
arcs.stage.trubyChangedDesire.ask:
What does your hero find out?
How does it change their goal?
arcs.stage.trubyPlan.name: Plan
arcs.stage.trubyPlan.hint: The hero works out how they will beat the opponent and reach the goal.
arcs.stage.trubyPlan.ask:
What is your hero's plan?
What do they need to make it work?
arcs.stage.trubyCounterattack.name: Opponent's Plan and Main Counterattack
arcs.stage.trubyCounterattack.hint: The opponent has a plan too. Show it, and start the attack on the hero.
arcs.stage.trubyCounterattack.ask:
What is the opponent's plan?
How do they strike first?
arcs.stage.trubyDrive.name: Drive
arcs.stage.trubyDrive.hint: The hero keeps going through a run of actions. As they start to lose, they start to do wrong to win.
arcs.stage.trubyDrive.ask:
What lengths does your hero go to?
Which line do they cross?
arcs.stage.trubyAttackByAlly.name: Attack by Ally
arcs.stage.trubyAttackByAlly.hint: An ally confronts the hero about the means they are using. The hero defends themselves and learns nothing yet.
arcs.stage.trubyAttackByAlly.ask:
Which ally objects?
How does your hero justify what they did?
arcs.stage.trubyApparentDefeat.name: Apparent Defeat
arcs.stage.trubyApparentDefeat.hint: The hero seems to have lost. This is the lowest point so far.
arcs.stage.trubyApparentDefeat.ask:
What makes the loss look final?
What does it cost your hero?
arcs.stage.trubySecondRevelation.name: Second Revelation and Decision
arcs.stage.trubySecondRevelation.hint: A new discovery gives the hero the energy to go on. Their desire and motive change again, and winning becomes an obsession.
arcs.stage.trubySecondRevelation.ask:
What gets your hero back on their feet?
How far will they go now?
arcs.stage.trubyAudienceRevelation.name: Audience Revelation
arcs.stage.trubyAudienceRevelation.hint: Let the reader learn something the hero doesn't know, usually who an ally or opponent really is.
arcs.stage.trubyAudienceRevelation.ask:
What does the reader learn before your hero does?
How does this change the scenes that follow?
arcs.stage.trubyThirdRevelation.name: Third Revelation and Decision
arcs.stage.trubyThirdRevelation.hint: The hero learns what they are really up against and decides how to fight. This is the last change of plan.
arcs.stage.trubyThirdRevelation.ask:
What does your hero finally learn about the opponent?
What is their last plan?
arcs.stage.trubyGauntlet.name: Gate, Gauntlet and Visit to Death
arcs.stage.trubyGauntlet.hint: The pressure closes in. The hero passes through a narrow place under attack and faces their own death.
arcs.stage.trubyGauntlet.ask:
Where does the conflict close in on your hero?
How do they face death, real or not?
arcs.stage.trubyBattle.name: Battle
arcs.stage.trubyBattle.hint: The final fight, physical or not. The hero and the opponent settle who wins.
arcs.stage.trubyBattle.ask:
Where does the final fight take place?
What is really being decided?
arcs.stage.trubySelfRevelation.name: Self-Revelation
arcs.stage.trubySelfRevelation.hint: The hero sees who they are and what they have done wrong. This is the emotional peak of the story.
arcs.stage.trubySelfRevelation.ask:
What does your hero admit to themselves?
What does it cost them to see it?
arcs.stage.trubyMoralDecision.name: Moral Decision
arcs.stage.trubyMoralDecision.hint: The hero proves the change with an action. They choose between two ways of acting, and the choice shows what they have learned.
arcs.stage.trubyMoralDecision.ask:
What choice does your hero face?
What does the choice prove?
arcs.stage.trubyNewEquilibrium.name: New Equilibrium
arcs.stage.trubyNewEquilibrium.hint: Everything returns to normal, on a higher or a lower level, depending on whether the hero has changed.
arcs.stage.trubyNewEquilibrium.ask:
What does normal look like now?
Is your hero better or worse off?
arcs.stage.proppAbsentation.name: Absentation
arcs.stage.proppAbsentation.hint: Someone leaves home or a family member is away, and the hero is left unprotected.
arcs.stage.proppAbsentation.ask:
Who is missing?
What does their absence leave open?
arcs.stage.proppInterdiction.name: Interdiction
arcs.stage.proppInterdiction.hint: The hero is told not to do something, or ordered to do it.
arcs.stage.proppInterdiction.ask:
What is your hero told?
Who tells them?
arcs.stage.proppViolation.name: Violation
arcs.stage.proppViolation.hint: The rule is broken, and the villain enters the story.
arcs.stage.proppViolation.ask:
How is the rule broken?
How does the villain arrive?
arcs.stage.proppReconnaissance.name: Reconnaissance
arcs.stage.proppReconnaissance.hint: The villain tries to learn something, such as where the treasure is or who the victim is.
arcs.stage.proppReconnaissance.ask:
What does the villain want to know?
How do they try to find out?
arcs.stage.proppDelivery.name: Delivery
arcs.stage.proppDelivery.ask:
What does the villain learn?
Who gives it away?
arcs.stage.proppTrickery.name: Trickery
arcs.stage.proppTrickery.hint: The villain tries to deceive the victim with a disguise, persuasion or magic.
arcs.stage.proppTrickery.ask: How does the villain deceive the victim?
arcs.stage.proppComplicity.name: Complicity
arcs.stage.proppComplicity.hint: The victim falls for it and helps the villain without meaning to.
arcs.stage.proppComplicity.ask: How does the victim help without knowing?
arcs.stage.proppVillainy.name: Villainy or Lack
arcs.stage.proppVillainy.hint: The villain harms a family member, or someone in the family lacks something they want.
arcs.stage.proppVillainy.ask:
What harm is done, or what is missing?
Who suffers from it?
arcs.stage.proppMediation.name: Mediation
arcs.stage.proppMediation.hint: The hero learns of the harm or the lack, and is sent or asked to act.
arcs.stage.proppMediation.ask:
How does your hero find out?
Who asks them to act?
arcs.stage.proppCounteraction.name: Beginning Counteraction
arcs.stage.proppDeparture.name: Departure
arcs.stage.proppDeparture.ask: What does your hero leave behind?
arcs.stage.proppDonorTest.name: Test by the Donor
arcs.stage.proppDonorTest.hint: Someone tests the hero, which prepares them to receive help or a magical gift.
arcs.stage.proppDonorTest.ask:
Who tests your hero?
What is the test?
arcs.stage.proppHeroReaction.name: The Hero's Reaction
arcs.stage.proppHeroReaction.hint: The hero passes or fails the test.
arcs.stage.proppHeroReaction.ask:
How does your hero respond?
What does the response show about them?
arcs.stage.proppMagicalAgent.name: Receipt of a Magical Agent
arcs.stage.proppMagicalAgent.hint: The hero gets a gift, a helper or a power.
arcs.stage.proppMagicalAgent.ask:
What does your hero receive?
What will it let them do?
arcs.stage.proppGuidance.name: Guidance
arcs.stage.proppGuidance.hint: The hero travels or is led to what they are looking for.
arcs.stage.proppGuidance.ask: How does your hero find the way?
arcs.stage.proppStruggle.name: Struggle
arcs.stage.proppStruggle.hint: The hero and the villain fight directly.
arcs.stage.proppStruggle.ask:
Where do they meet?
What kind of fight is it?
arcs.stage.proppBranding.name: Branding
arcs.stage.proppBranding.hint: The hero is marked, by a wound or a token.
arcs.stage.proppBranding.ask: What mark does your hero carry away?
arcs.stage.proppVictory.name: Victory
arcs.stage.proppLiquidation.name: Liquidation
arcs.stage.proppLiquidation.hint: The original harm or lack is put right.
arcs.stage.proppReturn.name: Return
arcs.stage.proppReturn.hint: The hero sets off for home.
arcs.stage.proppReturn.ask: How has your hero's view of home changed?
arcs.stage.proppPursuit.name: Pursuit
arcs.stage.proppPursuit.ask:
Who is after your hero?
Why now?
arcs.stage.proppRescue.name: Rescue
arcs.stage.proppRescue.hint: The hero escapes the pursuit or is saved from it.
arcs.stage.proppRescue.ask: How does your hero get away?
arcs.stage.proppUnrecognized.name: Unrecognized Arrival
arcs.stage.proppUnrecognized.hint: The hero arrives home or in another land, and nobody recognizes them.
arcs.stage.proppUnrecognized.ask:
Where does your hero arrive?
Why does nobody know them?
arcs.stage.proppUnfoundedClaims.name: Unfounded Claims
arcs.stage.proppUnfoundedClaims.hint: A false hero claims the hero's deeds.
arcs.stage.proppUnfoundedClaims.ask:
Who takes the credit?
Why do people believe them?
arcs.stage.proppDifficultTask.name: Difficult Task
arcs.stage.proppDifficultTask.hint: The hero is set a hard task.
arcs.stage.proppDifficultTask.ask: What task could only the true hero do?
arcs.stage.proppSolution.name: Solution
arcs.stage.proppSolution.ask: How does your hero do it?
arcs.stage.proppRecognition.name: Recognition
arcs.stage.proppRecognition.hint: The hero is recognized, often by the mark or the token.
arcs.stage.proppExposure.name: Exposure
arcs.stage.proppExposure.hint: The false hero or the villain is exposed.
arcs.stage.proppTransfiguration.name: Transfiguration
arcs.stage.proppTransfiguration.hint: The hero gets a new appearance, new clothes or a new standing.
arcs.stage.proppTransfiguration.ask: How does the world see your hero now?
arcs.stage.proppPunishment.name: Punishment
arcs.stage.proppWedding.name: Wedding
arcs.stage.proppWedding.hint: The hero marries, takes the throne or gets another reward.
arcs.stage.bookerAnticipation.name: Anticipation
arcs.stage.bookerAnticipation.hint: The hero is called to the adventure and looks ahead to what is coming.
arcs.stage.bookerAnticipation.ask:
What calls your hero away?
What do they expect to find?
arcs.stage.bookerDream.name: Dream
arcs.stage.bookerDream.hint: The adventure begins and goes well. The hero has some success and starts to feel they can't lose.
arcs.stage.bookerDream.ask:
What goes right for your hero?
Which illusion do they start to believe?
arcs.stage.bookerFrustration.name: Frustration
arcs.stage.bookerFrustration.hint: The hero meets the enemy for the first time, and the feeling of being unbeatable breaks.
arcs.stage.bookerFrustration.ask:
Who or what stops your hero?
Which illusion breaks?
arcs.stage.bookerNightmare.name: Nightmare
arcs.stage.bookerNightmare.hint: Things get worse until hope seems lost. This is the climax of the plot.
arcs.stage.bookerNightmare.ask:
What is the worst moment?
Why does all seem lost?
arcs.stage.bookerResolution.name: Resolution
arcs.stage.bookerResolution.hint: Against the odds, the hero overcomes the enemy.
arcs.stage.bookerResolution.ask:
How does your hero win?
What do they gain?
